content: Goal: pick a coupling position not used in prior rounds. Read: workspace listing only (no repo files read yet). Observed: prior rounds already covered behaviour-weighted Fréchet codebook (round 1), per-level curvature set by prefix transition score (CURVCTRL-SID), behaviour-ranked radial Poincare assignment (BRad-RQ), Lorentz successor-profile smoothing, behaviour cones, successor geodesic shift. Reasoning: four free positions remain distinct — (a) curved OT/Sinkhorn assignment, (b) curved residual chain, (c) gradient path / straight-through transport, (d) velocity fields on frames. I aim at (c) since none of the three rounds touched the *gradient path* of the RQ-VAE; a behaviour-directed Lorentz parallel-transported straight-through gradient is a different computational locus and has a clean 2x2 switch (behaviour-off / geometry-off / both-on). Open: write the minimal spec, safeguards, derived quantities (no tuning constants), cost at 24556 items, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs (72,000 steps).

IDEA: BG-LORENTZ-ST
TITLE: Behaviour-gated Lorentz parallel transport of the RQ-VAE straight-through gradient (curvature on the gradient path, not on the codebook)
MOTIVATION: In an RQ-VAE the encoder only ever receives the reconstruction straight-through gradient, so the latent geometry that fixes the SID prefixes is never told how users actually move between items; hubs near the Poincare origin and tail items near the boundary also get the same effective step size. This puts curvature and training-only transition behaviour *inside the gradient that shapes the codes*.
NOVELTY: Prior rounds changed the codebook (successor-weighted Frechet means), the per-level curvature (prefix-transition-score schedule) and the assignment radius (behaviour-ranked radial assignment). None touched the straight-through gradient path. Here the behaviour signal rotates the transported gradient in the tangent frame and the hyperbolic metric rescales it by radius; the quantizer and codebooks keep their existing Euclidean form.
CHANGE: The decoder->encoder straight-through gradient is lifted to the Lorentz model, parallel transported from the chosen code point back to the encoder tangent point, rotated in that tangent frame toward the item's successor direction by an angle derived from the item's successor entropy, and mapped back.
SPECIFICATION: see full block in final record.
COST: +1-3% wall clock; ~20k sparse gathers + O(B*d) map/transport/rotation per step at B~1023, 72,000 steps total.
HYPOTHESIS: on one run, per-level code usage entropy and prefix-collision behaviour shift, the cosine between transported and raw ST gradient tracks w_i, and Stage3 test_recall@10 rises above 0.065.
RISKS: optimizer trick with no objective anchoring; rotation may fight the reconstruction objective; sparse transition rows noisy.
END IDEA

IDEA: BG-LORENTZ-ST
TITLE: Behaviour-gated Lorentz parallel transport of the RQ-VAE straight-through gradient (curvature placed on the gradient path, not on the codebook)
MOTIVATION: In an RQ-VAE the encoder only ever receives the reconstruction straight-through (ST) gradient, so the latent geometry that fixes the SID prefixes is never told how users actually move between items, and hub items sitting near the Poincare origin get the same effective step size as tail items sitting near the boundary. This mechanism puts both the training-only transition behaviour and a real negative curvature inside the gradient that shapes the codes, so the prefix hierarchy is formed under a metric that is stretched toward successor structure.
NOVELTY: Earlier rounds changed the codebook (successor-weighted Frechet means), the per-level curvature schedule (prefix-transition score), and the assignment radius (behaviour-ranked radial assignment). None of them touched the straight-through gradient path. Here the quantizer, the residual chain and the codebooks keep their existing Euclidean form; the coupling lives in the transport, rotation and metric rescaling of the decoder-to-encoder gradient, which is a different computational locus from assignment, codebook update and residual geometry.
CHANGE: The decoder-side ST gradient is lifted to the Lorentz model at the quantized point, parallel transported along the geodesic to the encoder tangent point, rotated inside that tangent frame toward the item's behaviour-derived successor direction by an angle derived from the item's successor-pattern determinism, and mapped back to the encoder, so both the direction and the metric-scaled magnitude of the encoder update depend on behaviour and curvature jointly.
SPECIFICATION:
Notation: encoder output z (Euclidean, dim d), residual quantizer output q = sum_l c_{l,k_l} (Euclidean), decoder gradient g = dL_rec/dq, batch of B items per step, item index i, fixed curvature c_H = 1 (curvature K = -1, fixed, not trained), Lorentz hyperboloid H = {x : <x,x>_L = -1} with <x,y>_L = -x0*y0 + x.y.
Behaviour quantity per item i (training sequences only): successor distribution P_i over items, sparse, top-K (K = 20 documented default) after popularity back-off; determinism w_i = 1 - H(P_i)/log(n_i + 1), clipped to [0,1], H = Shannon entropy of P_i over its n_i retained successors, detached, EMA-smoothed (decay 0.99 documented default).
Geometry: exp_o(v) = (cosh s, sinh(s) v/s) with s = ||v|| (s < 1e-8 handled by Taylor), and its inverse log_o.
Successor tangent direction (EMA item-tangent table T, updated only with training-batch latents): d_i = sum_{j in supp(P_i)} P_i(j) * z_j^EMA, detached, unit-normalised, with 1e-8 floor.
Transport: x = exp_o(q), y = exp_o(z), u = PT_{x->y}(g_H) with PT_{x->y}(v) = v + <y,v>_L/(1 - <x,y>_L) * (x + y), g_H = (0, g) in the tangent at x.
Rotation: theta_i = (pi/2) * w_i (quarter turn ceiling, documented default); build an orthonormal pair e1 = normalise(u_tangent_part), e2 = normalise(d_i - <d_i,e1> e1); u' = ||u|| * (cos(theta_i) e1 + sin(theta_i) e2); g_enc = dlog_o|_y(u') in R^d (drop the timelike component, add it back if the target code adds it).
Loss/grad path: encoder receives g_enc in place of g (straight-through unchanged otherwise); reconstruction, commitment and codebook losses unchanged; no extra loss term.
Switches: BEH_OFF sets theta_i = 0 (pure transport); GEO_OFF replaces exp/log/PT by identity and the rotation by a Euclidean rota

tion in R^d (behaviour only); BOTH_ON is the full path above.
COST: At the frozen scale (24556 items, B ~ 1023, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs = 72,000 steps) the extra work per step is one sparse successor gather (<= 20 indices per item, ~20k floats), one exp/log pair, one Lorentz parallel transport (O(d)), one Gram-Schmidt rotation (O(d)) and one EMA table write (B*d); memory 24556 x d floats for the tangent table (~6.3 MB at d = 64) and 24556 x 20 int32 (~2 MB). Expected wall clock +1% to +3% over baseline, no extra backprop, no extra forward pass; total added cost over the run is well under one epoch of training.
HYPOTHESIS: If the SID prefixes are to be predictable by a generative next-item model, the code geometry must be stretched toward successor directions and tail items must receive larger metric-scaled steps; the run is worth keeping if (a) the per-item angle between g_enc and g grows monotonically with w_i, (b) per-level code usage entropy and the number of shared shallow prefixes between transition-linked items change relative to the recorded Euclidean baseline diagnostics, and (c) Stage3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065 in the single run.
RISKS: An optimizer-side rotation is not anchored in the objective, so the reconstruction loss may simply fight it back; noisy or nearly uniform transition rows make w_i small and the mechanism inert; the Lorentz conformal factor can amplify gradients for near-boundary tail items into instability unless clipped; if the EMA tangent table lags, the successor direction points at stale latents; a single run with seed noise may not resolve a small effect.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed item-to-item transition distribution of each training item, plus a popularity back-off, condensed into one scalar per item: the determinism (1 minus normalised successor entropy) of where users go after item i.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the training split only, one pass over consecutive pairs (u_t -> u_{t+1}) inside each training sequence; raw counts C_ij, back-off P_ij proportional to C_ij / (freq_j)^0.5 (0.5 is the documented default popularity exponent), rows renormalised, truncated to top-K = 20 successors, stored as a sparse CSR row per item; per-item successor entropy H(P_i) computed once in that pass and turned into w_i; the EMA item-tangent table z^EMA is updated from training-batch encoder outputs only.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: The transition matrix, the successor entropies w_i and the EMA tangent table are built exclusively from training-split sequences and training-batch forward passes; validation and test interactions are never read in any pass, and the SID vocabulary (all item codes) is frozen after Stage 2, so no validation or test interaction can influence assignment, curvature, or the transport used at inference; evaluation only consumes frozen SIDs.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Lorentz model on the hyperboloid of fixed curvature c_H = 1 (K = -1): exponential and logarithmic maps at the origin, geodesic parallel transport PT_{x->y}(v) = v + <y,v>_L/(1 - <x,y>_L)(x+y), and the induced metric rescaling of the tangent norm between x and y; the transported gradient is rotated inside the tangent frame at y by an angle derived from behaviour.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Entirely inside the straight-through gradient path of the RQ-VAE quantizer, i.e. between the decoder's gradient at the quantized code and the encoder's parameter update; it acts at every training step of Stage 2 and is identity at inference.
COUPLING PATH: behaviour ->

w_i and d_i -> rotation angle and rotation plane in the tangent frame at y -> rotated transported gradient -> single gradient vector returned to the encoder -> encoder parameters -> item latents -> SID codes; the transport is the only route by which the gradient reaches the encoder, so setting w_i = 0 removes the behaviour term and setting curvature to zero removes the transport and metric rescaling, and either change alters the returned gradient.
COUPLING EQUATION: g_enc = dlog_o|_y ( ||PT_{x->y}(g_H)|| * [ cos((pi/2) w_i) e1 + sin((pi/2) w_i) e2 ] ), with e1 = unit tangent part of PT_{x->y}(g_H) (the curved term) and e2 = unit successor direction d_i = sum_j P_ij z_j^EMA built from the behaviour term; BEH_OFF is w_i = 0, GEO_OFF is PT = identity and exp/log = identity with e1 = normalise(g).
OBSERVABLES: (1) per-item cosine between the returned encoder gradient and the raw ST gradient, which must decrease with increasing w_i and be exactly 1 in BEH_OFF; (2) the norm ratio ||g_enc||/||g|| as a function of the item's Lorentz radius, which must be flat in GEO_OFF; (3) per-level code usage entropy, per-level prefix counts and the number of transition-linked item pairs sharing a level-1 or level-2 prefix, recorded as diagnostics only; (4) final Stage3 test_recall@10 against the 0.065 target.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: w_i = 0 for all items, so theta = 0 everywhere and the gradient is only Lorentz-transported: the encoder update is metric-aware but blind to successor structure, and the recorded w_i-gradient correlation diagnostic collapses to zero.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: curvature set to zero (exp/log/PT replaced by identity, flat tangent), keeping the behaviour rotation in R^d: the encoder gradient direction depends on behaviour but the metric rescaling and geodesic transport are gone, so the radius-graded step size diagnostic becomes flat.
ABLATION BOTH ON: the full pathway, Lorentz transport with the behaviour-derived rotation, is the one trained run; the two switches exist in code, are unit-checked (BEH_OFF reproduces the pure transport, GEO_OFF reproduces the Euclidean rotated gradient, both must reduce to the exact baseline gradient when both are off), and no arm is trained with them off.
SPEC EQUATIONS:
  exp_o(v) = (cosh||v||, sinh(||v||) v/||v||);  log_o(x) = arccosh(-<x,o>_L)... with o = (1,0): log_o(x) = (arccosh(x0)) * x_{1:}/||x_{1:}||
  PT_{x->y}(v) = v + <y,v>_L / (1 - <x,y>_L) * (x + y)
  w_i = clip(1 - H(P_i)/log(n_i + 1), 0, 1);  theta_i = (pi/2) * w_i
  d_i = normalise( sum_{j in supp(P_i)} P_ij * T[j] )      # T = EMA item tangent table
  g_H = (0, g);  u = PT_{exp_o(q) -> exp_o(z)}(g_H)
  e1 = normalise(u[1:]);  e2 = normalise(d_i - <d_i,e1> e1)
  g_enc = J_log(y) @ ( ||u[1:]|| * (cos(theta_i) e1 + sin(theta_i) e2) )   # J_log = tangent map of log_o
  pseudocode per step:
    forward encoder -> z; quantize -> q (unchanged RQ-VAE)
    backward decoder -> g = dL/dq
    if GEO_OFF: u_par, w_scale = g, 1.0 else: u_par = PT(...)(g_H)[1:], w_scale = 1.0
    if BEH_OFF: theta, e2 = 0, None else: theta, e2 = (pi/2) w_i, successor direction
    g_enc = w_scale * ( cos(theta) * normalise(u_par) + sin(theta) * e2 ) * ||u_par||
    backprop encoder with g_enc; update T[i] <- 0.99 T[i] + 0.01 z_i (detached, training batch only)
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: decoder gradient g at the quantized code (B x d), encoder latent z (B x d), quantized code q (B x d), sparse successor rows P_i and entropies w_i for the batch item ids, EMA table T.

Output: g_enc (B x d), the single gradient vector handed to the encoder autograd node (plus the updated EMA rows); no change to the forward pass, codebooks or the SID vocabulary.
SAFEGUARDS: clamp all Lorentz points to x0 >= 1 + 1e-6 and ||x_{1:}|| <= sqrt(2 x0 1e-6) style radius cap so that ||x_{1:}|| <= 1 - 1e-5; compute PT and exp/log in float64 for that subgraph; Taylor branches for arccosh/sinh at small argument; if ||u[1:]|| < 1e-8 or <x,y>_L > 1 - 1e-6, fall back to the raw gradient; cap the transported norm ratio at the measured per-step 99th percentile of ||g|| (measured, not tuned) to stop near-boundary blow-up; w_i clipped to [0,1] and detached, P_i rows renormalised with a 1e-12 floor; items without a transition row get w_i = 0 and d_i = 0, which degrades exactly to a pure transport step; EMA table initialised from the first epoch's detached latents and never written at eval.
END IDEA
